 Keep a copy of your completed application.
 You must apply for this visa online. Most applicants must apply from outside Australia. You can only apply in Australia if you hold an eligible visa and meet an exemption category. You should submit a complete and decision-ready application. Applications that are lodged without relevant documentation may be refused or delayed. The application form in ImmiAccount tells you what documents to attach.
 If you are in Australia
-You can’t apply for a student visa in Australia if you hold a: Subclass 400 – Temporary Work (all streams) Subclass 403 – (Domestic Worker – Diplomatic/Consular stream) Subclass 407 – Training (all streams) Subclass 408 – Temporary Activity (all streams) Subclass 417 – Working Holiday (all streams) Subclass 457 – Temporary Work (all streams) Subclass 462 – Work and Holiday (all streams) Subclass 482 – Skills in Demand / Temporary Skill Shortage (all streams) Subclass 485 – Temporary Graduate Subclass 600 – Visitor Subclass 601 – ETA Subclass 602 – Medical Treatment Subclass 651 – eVisitor Subclass 771 – Transit Subclass 988 – Maritime Crew Subclass 995 – Diplomatic (Temporary) (Primary only. A family member of a Diplomatic (Temporary) visa (subclass 995) can apply for a Student visa in Australia). If you hold one of the visas on this list there are no exemptions to these rules. You may be able to apply for another Student visa while in Australia if you are a student visa holder. Dependent student visa holders are unable to apply for a student visa as the primary applicant while in Australia. For more information, see Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia in the Eligibility tab. If you don’t hold a substantive visa you may apply for a student visa within 28 days of holding a special purpose visa or a dependent Diplomatic (temporary) visa. You may also apply for a student visa in Australia within 28 days of being notified of an Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) decision if: your last substantive visa was a student visa your Student visa was cancelled the Student visa had already ceased by the time the ART set aside the cancellation decision you meet one of the exemptions to lodge a student visa application in Australia. You cannot make a valid application for a Student visa if you: do not hold a substantive visa, and you have previously been granted a visa based on an application made when you did not hold a substantive visa.
+You can’t apply for a student visa in Australia if you hold a: Subclass 400 – Temporary Work (all streams) Subclass 403 – (Domestic Worker – Diplomatic/Consular stream) Subclass 407 – Training (all streams) Subclass 408 – Temporary Activity (all streams) Subclass 417 – Working Holiday (all streams) Subclass 457 – Temporary Work (all streams) Subclass 462 – Work and Holiday (all streams) Subclass 482 – Skills in Demand / Temporary Skill Shortage (all streams) Subclass 485 – Temporary Graduate Subclass 600 – Visitor Subclass 601 – ETA Subclass 602 – Medical Treatment Subclass 651 – eVisitor Subclass 771 – Transit Subclass 988 – Maritime Crew Subclass 995 – Diplomatic (Temporary) (Primary only. A family member of a Diplomatic (Temporary) visa (subclass 995) can apply for a Student visa in Australia). If you hold one of the visas on this list there are no exemptions to these rules. You may be able to apply for another Student visa while in Australia if you are a student visa holder. Dependent student visa holders are unable to apply for a student visa as the primary applicant while in Australia. For more information, see Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia in the Eligibility tab. If you don’t hold a substantive visa you may apply for a student visa within 28 days of holding a special purpose visa or a dependent Diplomatic (temporary) visa. You may also apply for a student visa in Australia within 28 days of being notified of an Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) decision if: your last substantive visa was a student visa your Student visa was cancelled the Student visa had already ceased by the time the ART set aside the cancellation decision. You cannot make a valid application for a Student visa if you: do not hold a substantive visa, and you have previously been granted a visa based on an application made when you did not hold a substantive visa.
 Do not provide false and misleading information
 Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.
 Create or log in to ImmiAccount Attach documents Pay the visa application charge Paying the application charge When you submit your application you must: pay for you and your family members or your application will not be valid or provide proof of exemption as shown in 'Step by step', Gather your documents. If your visa cancellation was set aside by the Tribunal you can’t apply online. Instead submit a ImmiAccount technical support form. Note: a valid application must be made within the eligibility timeframe as late applications will not be accepted. See how to resolve error messages when submitting online. Note: If you are eligible to include dependents in your application, we cannot grant a Student visa to your child if they are 18 years or over at the time your visa is finished. Instead, they should apply for their own visa.
